ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, directors, officers and ultimate beneficial owners at onboarding against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List and associated terrorism-financing resolutions; (ii) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list; (iii) the EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists; and (iv) Panama's UAF list of linked and blocked persons under Law No. 23 of 2015, as updated. Foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, beneficial-ownership corroboration through SIRE, and senior-management approval prior to execution of incorporation documents; any confirmed sanctions match or unexplained PEP profile constitutes automatic grounds for refusal of service.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - online name-search and reservation services available through the eRegistro platform and the official website of the Public Registry (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa and related e-service modules)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name need not be Spanish but must be expressible in Latin-alphabet characters accepted by the Public Registry; Spanish is the operational language of registration instruments. The name must be exclusive, not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity in Panama, and must be accompanied by the denomination Sociedad Anónima or the abbreviation S.A. (or a recognized equivalent corporate designation) pursuant to Law No. 32 of 1927.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant files a written Recurso de Reconsideración with the Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá within five (5) business days of notification under Ley No. 38 of 2000, attaching the name-search certificate and evidence of compliance with naming rules. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file a further Recurso de Apelación within five (5) business days to the superior administrative instance of the Public Registry; exhaustion of administrative remedies preserves the right to judicial review before the Tercera Sala of the Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for statutory purposes: a Panama S.A. may maintain the resident agent's qualifying address as its statutory registered office. For the FDA/CE medical-device regulatory-consulting activity, a virtual business-center address is acceptable for registration and bank onboarding, provided the entity demonstrates verifiable commercial substance through management functions, executed client contracts, bank statements, and RUC tax filings. Mail-forwarding and call-answering services through the resident agent or a serviced-office provider satisfy the low-risk standard, with a full physical office recommended only when revenue or payroll levels increase.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 5% probability of unannounced physical inspection during the first 24 months for a standard-risk MedTech consulting entity. DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) and UAF inspections are risk-targeted and would materialize primarily upon inconsistent tax reporting, missing RUC filings, PEP-related red flags, or customer AML complaints.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 32 of 1927 (Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas), as amended by Law No. 5 of 2019 and related supplementary provisions; applicable articles concerning incorporation, corporate name, registered office, registered agent, capital shares, directors, and corporate records.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección del Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. The articles of incorporation must state a nominal subscribed capital chosen by the incorporators; shares may be issued for such consideration as the Board of Directors determines under Panamanian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST, that the Board of Directors approves the subscription and issuance of [number] common shares at par value [amount] to the founding shareholders and accepts payment of the aggregate subscription price. RESOLVED SECOND, that the registered office of the corporation is established at [address, Panama City, Republic of Panama], and the registered agent named in the Articles of Incorporation is ratified. RESOLVED THIRD, that the following officers be and hereby are appointed: [Name], President; [Name], Treasurer; and [Name], Secretary. The Secretary shall certify these resolutions and the President is authorized to execute all documents necessary to finalize corporate incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección del Mercantil (online portal: Registro Público en Línea)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the online corporate name application on the Registro Público de Panamá e-services portal. Indicate one preferred name and up to three alternatives in Spanish, and select the entity type 'Sociedad Anónima'. Make the prescribed search payment. Once the name reservation certificate is issued, use it within its validity period, typically thirty working days, when executing the incorporation deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, file a reconsideration brief with supporting evidence of prior use or file a new reservation under a distinct name before the expiry of the original application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Public Incorporation Deed before a Panamanian Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panama Notary Public duly licensed to authenticate corporate instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Spanish-language Pacto Social y Estatutos, specifying the corporate name, business object, share structure, registered office, registered agent, and initial directors or officers. Execute the deed before a Panamanian notary. The notary authenticates the signatures of the incorporators and the registered agent's acceptance, and produces first certified copies for the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Passport copy or identity card of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies omissions or inconsistencies, correct the deficient clauses and re-execute the deed; any superseded notarial copies are destroyed and replaced by the corrected public instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit and Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección del Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the first certified copy of the executed public deed, the original name reservation certificate, and proof of payment of registry fees and protocol stamps at the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry. The Registrar reviews the corporate clauses for legal compliance, assigns a mercantile folio, and records the incorporation entry.
required_dossiers: First certified copy of executed public incorporation deed
Proof of payment of stamp taxes and public registry fees
Mercantile registration cover sheet, if required by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner issues a note of defect, remedy the defect within the applicable statutory cure period, ordinarily fifteen working days, and resubmit the corrected document; otherwise the registration application is archived and a new filing must be made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Certified Evidence of Incorporation and Corporate Standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certifications Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registration entry is granted, request from the Certifications Desk a certified copy of the registered deed and a certificate of legal existence of the corporation. Verify that the certificate accurately reflects the corporate name, registered office, registered agent, directors, and share capital. Use these documents for banking and downstream corporate formalities.
required_dossiers: Mercantile folio number assigned to the corporation
Written request or certification application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains inaccurate particulars, submit a corrective application with the mercantile folio and supporting documents, or request a certified copy of the original registered deed for reconciliation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization Meeting, Share Subscription Ratification, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate in-house governance; no government filing is required for the organizational meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the initial shareholder meeting or obtain unanimous written consent to ratify the share subscription and elect directors. The Board then adopts the first board resolution approving the share issuance, adopting the registered office and registered agent, and appointing officers. The Secretary records the meetings in the corporate minute book and updates the share ledger.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum or consent defect exists, convene a duly noticed adjourned meeting or obtain a unanimous written consent in accordance with the bylaws and Law No. 32 of 1927.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Creation of Corporate Records, Share Ledger, and Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary and registered agent; not a government filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporation's minute book, share register ledger, and issued share certificates. Have the President and Secretary sign the certificates for subscribed shares. Ensure the share ledger records each shareholder, number of shares, date of issue, and consideration received. Retain the corporate records at the registered office in Panama as required by Law No. 32 of 1927.
required_dossiers: Director and shareholder signature specimen records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If share certificates or ledger entries contain errors, void the defective certificates and execute replacement certificates; if the ledger is defective, prepare corrected pages and obtain fresh certification from the Corporate Secretary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the MedTech regulatory consulting activity does not involve industrial production in Panama and is not subject to an industrial manufacturing license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; FDA 510(k) filing and European CE-mark compliance consulting is a non-regulated professional service. Only a standard municipal operating permit (Aviso de Operación) is triggered if a physical consulting office is opened.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — non-industrial professional consultancy services are not listed among activities requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment in Panama.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated by non-industrial regulatory consulting operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A physical office, if established, must comply with ordinary workplace occupancy rules. Obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, a municipal use and operation permit (Aviso de Operación) from the relevant municipality, and workplace safety clearance under the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL). No civil-defense or structural-load license applies to a professional consultancy office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; Sede Electrónica (e-Tax Portal) at https://www.dgi.gob.pa and https://etax-dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Sociedad Anónima at the Registro Público de Panamá through a licensed resident agent and obtain the certified incorporation records. Step 2: File the municipal Aviso de Operación with the Circuito Municipal of the registered office. Step 3: Register online via the DGI Sede Electrónica to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), submitting the certificate of incorporation, resident agent acceptance, director/shareholder identification (passport copies), and proof of registered address. Step 4: Activate tax obligations in the e-Tax account: corporate income tax (ISR), ITBMS (VAT), dividends withholding, RAI (animated corporation tax) payment, and advance/estimated ISR declarations; Sede Electrónica issues the RUC resolution within 1-3 business days for non-resident-owned S.A. entities. Non-resident shareholders and directors are permitted and may delegate local filing acts to the resident agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope (No_Pass_Through). Panama S.A. is taxed at entity level on Panama-source income only; foreign-source income is exempt; the entity is treated as a per-se corporation for U.S. tax purposes and cannot elect partnership pass-through treatment; no Tax_Exempt_Zone treatment arises automatically, except where the S.A. opts into special regimes such as SEM headquarters, Free Zone, or Panama-Pacifico licensing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists on the Panamanian side. Available statutory elections include: (a) consolidated group filing election by affiliated companies (Art. 699-A Código Fiscal); (b) election to apply the Simplified Regime (Régimen Simplificado) at 2% of gross receipts for small-scale operations; (c) election between the standard 25% ISR bracket schedule and presumptive taxation for taxpayers failing adequate accounting records; (d) optional ITBMS registration for service exporters whose annual transfers fall below the statutory threshold so they may lawfully issue 0% export invoices; and (e) election to apply the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime for regional MedTech consulting services, which grants special tax incentives and enhanced territorial benefits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (VAT/GST hybrid, Código Fiscal Arts. 1654 et seq. as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (Balboas 36,000; equivalent to USD 36,000) of annual gross taxable transfers gives rise to mandatory ITBMS registration; export-only service providers may register voluntarily to access the export zero-rating mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) implemented by DGI Resolution 201-0446/2019 and successive amendments; all invoices must be issued through DGI-validated billing software (Proveedor Tecnológico de Facturación, PTF) with real-time online transmission and assignment of a unique ministerial fiscal validation number; invoices carry a QR code and DGI control code; monthly electronic annexure and filing of the ITBMS return (Formulario mensual) through Sede Electrónica are mandatory. No traditional physical fiscal stamps remain operative for standard commercial invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% ITBMS applies to export services where the recipient is a non-resident, the service is performed from Panama but is wholly consumed or economically exploited outside Panamanian territory, and payment originates from abroad. FDA 510(k) filing and European CE Mark regulatory consulting sold to foreign medical device sponsors qualify if the deliverables (regulatory submissions, technical files, dossiers) are made available abroad and the client has no Panamanian permanent establishment or local taxable engagement. Eligibility is conditioned on prior filing of the export service registration/aviso with the DGI and ability to evidence foreign utilization; the same regime preserves the territorial ISR exemption for foreign-source consulting income. Panama has no foreign-exchange control, hence no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure stated under this schema is used only as a documentary discipline target for inward remittance evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DGI-validated export service registration (aviso/declaración de exportación de servicios) filed via Sede Electrónica
0%-rated electronic invoice bearing the DGI fiscal control code and QR with ITBMS zero-rate legend
Signed consulting agreement / statement of work with the foreign sponsor evidencing foreign utilization
Proof of foreign execution: submitted FDA 510(k) eCopy transmission or EU CE Mark dossier lodged with a Notified Body/competent authority
Inward remittance certificate and SWIFT payment evidence from the overseas client
Annual export-services reconciliation forming part of the income tax return (Formulario 330) and ITBMS monthly return
Corporate records supporting territorial sourcing if the DGI requests an economic substance demonstration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI can retroactively claw back zero-rating within the general 4-year audit window where the exporter fails to substantiate foreign use, foreign client residence, or foreign-source payment; re-characterized invoices are taxed at 7% plus monthly interest of 1% (Art. 1118 Código Fiscal) and late-payment surcharges; false export documentation or artificially routed service-export schemes attract fines up to 200% of the underpaid tax and administrative sanctions; deliberate fiscal fraud on zero-rated exports is criminally actionable under Panamanian law with imprisonment of up to 10 years. Export invoices must be matched to bank wire receipts and retain the full documentation bundle for the statutory retention period to avoid penalty and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system and maintains no traditional central bank. Banking and FX surveillance is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); AML/CFT supervision is conducted by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) acts as the fiscal and financial agent of the State. The US dollar is legal tender, and the Panamanian balboa (PAB) circulates only as coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity with the USD, thereby eliminating monetary policy, reserve requirements, and exchange-rate intervention by national authorities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama imposes no exchange-control legislation: both the current account and the capital account are fully convertible for residents and non-residents alike. Inbound foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, service fees, dividends, and intra-group payments can be freely credited, debited, and remitted in USD or any convertible currency without prior central bank approval, repatriation license, or destination-specific clearance. Profit remittance by a Sociedad Anónima is unrestricted from a treasury standpoint; the only practical gatekeeper is the commercial bank's own risk-based KYC/CDD framework, which requires transparent economic purpose and clear SWIFT payment references. Because the entity is territorial for income tax purposes, no FX control does or can impede the movement of consulting fees from FDA/CE clients in the United States or the European Union.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama maintains no export proceeds surrender regime, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline because the domestic economy is denominated in USD. The MedTech regulatory consulting company (ISIC 7490) may invoice its advisory services in USD, EUR, or any conventional currency and retain 100% of proceeds in its Panamanian operational account; no conversion into balboas is required or even commercially functional. If EUR-denominated CE-mark filing fees are collected, the company may either hold EUR in a multicurrency account or execute an immediate spot conversion into USD at the bank's daily telex rate.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for transaction collection only; LOW for deposit concentration or treasury function. Under SBP General Rule 004-2010 and the SBP Fintech Innovation Hub framework, a foreign electronic money institution (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Merco) may not hold Panamanian deposits, maintain a local settlement account, or act as the primary bank of a Panamanian S.A. without a full banking or fintech license issued by the SBP. A practical derived-rail architecture is permissible: the consulting company may use an offshore EMI exclusively to collect EUR/USD card and wire fees from FDA/CE clients, provided funds are auto-swept on a strict daily basis into the Panamanian operational account via MT103; the EMI will not appear as the corporate bank of record for statutory or tax registry purposes. Panamanian payroll, vendor payments, and tax obligations must execute through a tier-1 local bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A fully remote account opening without any Panama footprint is generally rejected for a non-resident-owned S.A. The SBP's risk-based CDD requires account officers to verify the legal representative, the directors, and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO); in practice, at least one in-person meeting must occur in Panama, normally attended by the registered agent or a lawful attorney-in-fact appointed by the company. UBOs who are not physically present must undergo a contracted video-identification call and, for medium-risk profiles such as a MedTech consulting firm, submit apostilled passports plus a bank reference from their home jurisdiction. Where the client is a professional services firm with no physical goods movement, banks may approve the account within 3-6 weeks if the company simultaneously maintains a registered office, a Panamanian resident agent (e.g., a law firm), and a documented beneficial-ownership register filed with the UAF.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: the company uses a Panama Foundation (PIF) or bearer-share structure, preventing the bank from identifying the real controller of the consulting operation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (a) a certified copy of the beneficial-ownership declaration filed with the UAF, (b) the notarized foundation charter/by-laws or share ledger certifying the founder/protector/council members, (c) a formal legal opinion from a Panamanian attorney confirming the economic ownership chain, (d) passports and proof of address of all natural-person UBOs, and (e) a corporate resolution approving the account mandate and the commercial plan of the FDA/CE consultancy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance red flag: non-resident directors, no local employees, and the use of a registered agent as the only physical connection to Panama.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a signed office-lease or subcontract with a licensed corporate-service provider, a real payroll plan for at least one Panama-based compliance administrator, projected-income financial statements, engagement letters with FDA/CE clients proving substantive professional activity, and a board resolution establishing substance steps within the next 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire-pattern alert: multiple incoming international payments classified as 'consulting' from US/EU medical device manufacturers without visible substrate documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a per-client invoice ledger with supporting FDA 510(k) submission correspondence, EMA/CE certificate references, signed consulting agreements, the ISIC/NAICS scope statement ('Medical Device Regulatory Consulting'), and monthly reconciliation statements that tie each wire to a named submission milestone.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume credit-card receipts from online acquiring processors (Stripe, PayPal) paired with limited correspondent-wire traffic, signaling possible pass-through or third-party payment laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Install a roll-forward transaction monitoring workbook, export the processor's merchant settlement reports showing client names and card reference numbers, evidence of refund-control policies (refunds only to the original card), and a compliance undertaking to maintain the acquirer's merchant account exclusively in the legal name of the Panamanian S.A.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the Treasury Blueprint, initial shareholder funding flows through SWIFT MT103 from the UBO's home account to the Panamanian operating account. Panama imposes no exchange-control filings, so no official purpose-code certification is required by the State; however, the receiving bank's compliance system demands a precise economic reference in Field 70, in particular 'Capital Contribution – Share Subscription' or 'Shareholder Loan Disbursement' if the injection is a bilateral loan. Large subscriptions above USD 250,000 may trigger a request for the shareholders register, a board resolution, the UAF beneficial-ownership certificate, and a 12-month source-of-funds statement. When the injection originates from a New York correspondent bank (e.g., Citi, JPMorgan, Bank of America), the USD credit posts on the same day; EUR capital injections are converted under a one-leg spot at the receiving bank's rate and booked in the US-dollar statement. For small working-capital top-ups, the entity may also receive funds via card acquire rails (Stripe or PayPal) provided those receipts are supported by genuine client invoices for regulatory advisory services.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Because the company is a professional consulting firm (ISIC 7490, NAICS 541690) with no physical goods movement, the primary outbound rail is the standard corporate SWIFT MT103 for vendor payments (subcontracted testing laboratories, translation/localization vendors, EU regulatory consultants, software subscriptions, payroll, tax, and retention of legal counsel). Commercial Letters of Credit are structurally unnecessary when no title documents or transit goods exist; a standby Letter of Credit or bank guarantee may be issued by Banco General or Banistmo only where a European client's procurement protocol requires a repayment guarantee, though this remains an exceptional instrument rather than a standing rail. Card-scheme disbursements (e.g., corporate credit card for FDA user fees and EU filing payments) settle through the VISA/Mastercard infrastructure and are funded directly from the same operational account, preserving a clean audit trail between inbound contest fees and outbound regulatory disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forwards (up to 12-month tenor) executed through the treasury desk of Banistmo (Grupo Bancolombia) or BAC International Bank, booked under an FX Master Agreement with no mandatory ISDA for notional amounts below USD 250,000.
Rolling FX swaps (spot against forward) to align the timing mismatch between EUR-denominated CE-mark invoice receipts and USD-denominated FDA filing disbursements.
Overnight cross-currency sweeps (tom-next quotes) to avoid idle EUR balances while retaining conversion optionality.

EUR/USD option collar strategies (zero-premium) available through the securities broker-dealers of Grupo Bancolombia or BAC under an SMV-authorized derivatives framework, permissible for hedging confirmed receivable pipelines.

Currency swaps (fixed-principal exchange) are permissible only under a full ISDA/CSA with the parent-bank treasury (Bancolombia or BAC) and are not required at the expected transaction volumes of the consulting operation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are explicitly not applicable and not necessary: the PAB is coin-only at a fixed 1:1 parity with USD, and Panama has no offshore non-convertibility constraint; any counterparty quoting a PAB NDF is pricing USD itself.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) through the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of USD 50 plus 10% annual interest; after 90 days of delinquency, the company is administratively stricken from the Public Registry and loses legal capacity until reinstated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público) via the designated Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Annual Franchise Tax; by January 31 annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain updated resident agent and office records may trigger administrative strike-off, forfeiture of corporate rights, and a reinstatement fee established by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Panama-source Income Tax Return in Respect of Panama-earned Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months following the end of the fiscal year, plus extensions as published annually by DGI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 10% on unpaid tax, interest at DGI's official rate, and fines up to USD 5,000; persistent non-filing may lead to registration cancellation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory external audit required if the Panama corporation has annual gross income from Panama-source business exceeding USD 2,000,000, holds a concession or license that requires audited financial statements, or is a regulated financial intermediary; other corporations may be exempt from independent audit but must maintain internal financial records.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS Standards for entities required to file statutory financial statements in Panama; simplified Local GAAP may be used for non-publicly accountable small corporations with no legal requirement to publish financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 23 of 2015 (as amended), the licensed Resident Agent must keep updated beneficial ownership records and must file the Annual UBO Confirmation when ownership changes occur; there is no separate standalone annual UBO register filing for standard S.A. corporations, but the registered agent must confirm that current UBO details are accurate as part of the annual franchise fee process.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 10,000 per year for a certified audit.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.00% on taxable net income derived from Panama-source activities (territorial tax system).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-source income, including consulting fees for regulatory services performed and economically realized outside Panama, is excluded from the Panamanian tax base under the territoriality principle. Full or preferential exemptions apply under designated regimes such as the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007, Panama Pacifico, and the Colon Free Zone. Small taxpayers with annual gross revenue up to USD 100,000 may apply the proportional reduced rates established by Cabinet Decree No. 27 of 2018.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1023 (Declaracion Jurada del Impuesto Sobre la Renta para Personas Juridicas) filed through the DGI Electronic Tax Portal (e-Tax 2.0); advance payments are remitted via Formulario 1015.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within the first three calendar months following the close of the fiscal year-end, i.e., by 31 March for calendar-year taxpayers; no automatic extension is available beyond the statutory period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ten-digit taxpayer registration number (RUC) with check digit, digital signature certificate, and updated commercial aviso de operacion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must appoint a resident legal representative to register the RUC and sign all sworn declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year covered by the return, stated in YYYY format.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The fiscal period must match the corporate accounting books physically maintained in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from activities carried out in Panama or capital employed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude fees for services performed abroad unless the consulting contract designates Panama as the place of performance; maintain executed contracts and invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income excluded under the territorial rule or under free-zone and SEM exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends paid out of exempt profits remain subject to the 10% withholding when repatriated to shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs of sales or services directly attributable to the revenue reported on Line 101.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only costs incurred to generate Panama-source income are deductible for territorial tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary expenses, including wages, rent, software licenses, subcontracted consulting fees, depreciation, and insurance, supported by valid receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to related foreign parties must be supported by transfer pricing documentation when the statutory threshold is met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source income less approved costs, operating expenses, and the applicable five-year loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled corporations must apply the territorial allocation rules consistently with their global books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax (ISR) computed at the 25% statutory rate on the net taxable income of Line 120.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Creditable advance payments, direct payments, and client withholdings reduce the gross tax computed here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly advance payments filed on Form 1015 and for taxes withheld by clients on Panama-source invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned corporations must evidence timely advance payments even when no final tax is due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 150 / Net Tax Payable or Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Excess of Line 130 over Line 140; payment is due in balboas or US dollars at the time of filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be remitted from a Panamanian bank account; repatriation of surplus is unrestricted under the dollarized currency regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Attachments / CPA Dictamen and TP Annex
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certified public accountant report (Dictamen de Contador Publico Autorizado) and, where applicable, the informative related-party disclosure annex.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The CPA must hold a valid Panamanian license; transfer pricing studies must be prepared in Spanish and retained for inspection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fine of 3% to 5% of the tax due per fiscal month of delay, capped at 100% to 150% of the tax; unpaid tax accrues a 5% monthly surcharge capped at 50% plus default interest at the annual rate fixed by the DGI. Other consequences include suspension of the RUC, embargo of bank accounts, denial of municipal and public-registry certificates, and publication in the official registry of tax delinquents.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding on dividends distributed from both taxed profits and non-taxed profits (exempt or foreign-source). The paying corporation may elect to absorb the 10% tax, in which case the dividend is treated as franked and no further shareholder withholding applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double-tax agreement, the Panamanian corporation must (1) obtain the DGI-issued Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) evidencing Panama tax residence; (2) submit the TRC together with a beneficial-ownership certificate to the foreign payer; (3) complete the source-state's treaty relief form to apply the reduced rate; and (4) renew the TRC annually, demonstrating substantive economic activity in Panama to survive treaty anti-abuse and limitation-on-benefits clauses.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties, technical-assistance fees, and know-how payments to non-residents are subject to a 12.5% statutory withholding under the Fiscal Code. Interest paid to foreign financial institutions on capital imports is generally exempt, while interest paid to non-cooperative or unregistered related lenders attracts 12.5%. Where a comprehensive DTA applies, such as with Mexico or South Korea, treaty rates may reduce royalty and interest withholding to 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.4,000,000 (four million Panamanian Balboas, at par with the US dollar) of annual gross revenue, or aggregate related-party transactions exceeding B/.4,000,000 in a fiscal year, triggers the mandatory preparation of Master File and Local File together with the annual informative related-party return under Law 50 of 2011 and Executive Decree No. 310 of 2012.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama applies substance-over-form and general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR). A corporation is treated as a Panama tax resident when management and control are exercised from Panama under Article 860 of the Fiscal Code, as reinforced by Law 66 of 2014. For SEM and free-zone beneficiaries, Economic Substance Regulations require physical premises, local staff, and substantive revenue-generating activity in Panama. Treaty benefits, dividend relief, and territorial exclusions are denied to shell entities lacking economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Panama-source consulting revenues, such as unrecorded FDA 510(k) and CE Mark compliance fees charged to US or EU clients, using false invoices issued by shell suppliers, or destroying accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud is punishable by imprisonment of 2 to 6 years, aggravated to 5 to 10 years when committed through fictitious companies or forged documents; civil penalty of 100% to 300% of the evaded tax; default interest; surcharges; and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and directors who sign the sworn return expose personal criminal liability; courts authorize piercing the corporate veil, freezing personal bank accounts, imposing travel bans, and extradition; unpaid taxes attach personally where the corporation is liquidated without settling DGI claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Panamanian Sociedad Anonima as a letterbox entity with no office, no local staff, no accounting books, and no records of consulting deliverables, used solely to receive non-taxable foreign-source funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization as a Panama tax resident under the control-and-management test of Article 860 of the Fiscal Code; retroactive assessments with penalties of 100% to 300%; denial of treaty and territorial benefits; fines for failure to maintain books; and cancellation of the corporate registration at the Registro Publico de Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid income tax and penalties; criminal responsibility arises when signing declarations of non-activity in bad faith; individuals may be disqualified from serving as directors of Panamanian entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving wire-transfer payments for purported regulatory consulting without substantive deliverables, layering funds through multiple shell S.A. entities, converting receipts into crypto assets, or servicing opaque or sanctioned beneficial owners contrary to Law 23 of April 27, 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is punishable by imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and fines equal to twice the value of the property involved; administrative penalties include suspension of the commercial license and forced dissolution of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and resident agents involved face personal criminal prosecution, asset freezes, passport seizure, travel bans, and extradition; the corporate veil is disregarded in predicate-offense proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and False Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing intercompany FDA/CE consulting services provided to a related US or EU parent, failing to file the informative related-party return when revenue exceeds B/.4,000,000, or submitting false transfer pricing analyses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may re-determine the arm's-length result with a secondary adjustment and impose penalties of 30% to 50% of the recomputed tax difference; additional fines apply for non-filing of the transfer pricing annex; the taxpayer is published in the official registry of tax delinquents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors attesting false transfer pricing documentation are personally liable for fraudulent misstatement; the foreign parent may face deemed dividend treatment; travel bans and asset embargos are imposed pending clearance of substantial assessments.
